text:
customer-ben: Hi team — onboarding POC is almost done, but two issues: 1) logs from our onprem app aren't making it into Datadog/Redwood stream (we use fluent-bit), and 2) traces in Console show spans but no parent trace (traceparent missing). We're blocked for the exec demo tomorrow.

sofia: @customer-ben sorry to hear that. Are you using Redwood managed drain or self-hosted connector? Also paste the fluent-bit output section if possible.

customer-ben: Self-hosted. Output config (redacted):

```ini
[OUTPUT]
    Name   http
    Match  redwood.*
    Host   logs.redwood.internal
    Port   443
    TLS    On
    Header Authorization Bearer REDACTED
    URI    /ingest/v1/events
```

mark: Quick thought: fluent-bit http output uses OpenSSL in the image; if your org intercepts TLS with an internal proxy that resigns certs, you need to provide the proxy CA via `tls.verify off` (not ideal) or mount the proxy CA cert into the container and point `tls.ca_file`. Any TLS errors in the fluent-bit logs?

customer-ben: I grepped the connector pod logs and saw: `ERR: SSL_connect: certificate verify failed` and a repeated `http: send failed, retrying`.

claire: From a security perspective we prefer not to disable TLS verification. Mounting the internal CA as a secret is fine. We can create a k8s secret `dd-proxy-ca` and mount to `/etc/ssl/redwood-proxy-ca.pem`.

mark: Also for traces, our runtime looks for `traceparent` (W3C) or `x-trace-id`. If your app is only sending `request-id` or `X-Correlation-ID`, that won't link spans automatically. Two options: 1) have the app set `traceparent` header with W3C format, or 2) add an Envoy header transform on the ingress to translate your header to `traceparent` or `x-trace-id`.

customer-ben: Our app sends `X-Correlation-ID: cid-789`. We can add an Envoy transform but need the exact glue.

mark: Envoy config snippet (add to request_headers_to_add): `- header: { key: "traceparent", value: "%REQ(X-CORRELATION-ID)%" }` — note that W3C traceparent requires a specific format, so a better short-term mapping is: `x-trace-id: %REQ(X-CORRELATION-ID)%` which our collectors accept.

infra-bot: Alert: connector-pod (namespace-poc) restart_count=3 in last 10m due to SSL verify error.

customer-ben: After mounting the CA and adding `x-trace-id` mapping I still see gaps: some events arrive but the Console shows `trace_id` present only for 60% of events.

sofia: Two follow-ups: 1) Are some clients bypassing the ingress (direct to runtime)? 2) Are you sampling traces at the app or sidecar level? If app-level sampling is on, searches will miss some trace_ids.

customer-ben: We do have a local sampler set to 50% for load reasons. But even when we force sampling we still have some `trace_id: null` in the raw ingest files.

mark: Check the ingest payload JSON — our runtime only populates `trace_id` when the incoming event payload or headers include `trace_id`, `x-trace-id`, or `traceparent`. If your sidecar sometimes batches multiple HTTP requests into a single payload and loses per-request headers, that could clear trace_id. Fluent-bit batch mode can do that. What's your `Batch` and `Compress` settings?

customer-ben: We're using `Batch=On` and `Compress=true` to save bandwidth. Could that strip headers?

mark: It can. Fluent-bit concatenates records; if you're forwarding as a single JSON array without preserving original HTTP headers per record, our ingest pipeline won't see per-record headers. Try setting `Batch` off or enable record transformers to copy `X-Correlation-ID` into the record body before batching. Example filter:

```ini
[FILTER]
    Name    modify
    Match   redwood.*
    Copy    1
    Key     $REQUEST_HEADERS.X-Correlation-ID
    New_key x_trace_id
```

customer-ben: Good tip. We'll attempt that. Also, while testing load we saw frequent 502s from the Redwood endpoint when bursts happened. Any guidance?

mark: 502s during burst usually mean the backend pool hit concurrency limits and Envoy returned 502. For POC, you can enable a retry policy with jitter and exponential backoff on the fluent-bit side (the http output supports `retry_limit` and `backoff_ms`). Also check Console -> Routes -> stats for `upstream_5xx` to see which service is failing.

claire: For the exec demo, you should tighten security for the CA mount and rotate the token after POC. We'll arrange a short sweep after the demo.

customer-ben: Plan of action I've got so far: 1) Mount internal proxy CA into fluent-bit via k8s secret and set `tls.ca_file` 2) Add Envoy header transform mapping `X-Correlation-ID` -> `x-trace-id` 3) Disable batching or copy header into record body before batching 4) Add retry/backoff to fluent-bit http output and watch upstream 5xx in Console. Is that reasonable?

sofia: Yes, solid. If you want, we can pair with an engineer for 30m now — mark is available.

customer-ben: Please. Booking now.

mark: I'll join and we can tail the connector logs, watch the Console canary stream I enabled for your org, and verify `trace_id` propagation.

customer-ben: After the pair we saw immediate improvement: TLS verified, logs flowing, and trace_id present for incoming events after moving the header into the record. Remaining action: adjust sampler and confirm no downstream token throttles. Thanks all.

sofia: Great — closing loop. We'll follow up with a short runbook (fluent-bit CA mount + filter snippet + Envoy header examples).

customer-ben: Perfect. Appreciate the help!
